comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Serialize the cap check with seat registration**

When two `--add-worker` processes start with three of four seats, both can complete this count before either new worktree has acquired its agmsg identity, so both observe `seats == 3`, pass the check, and subsequently register different workers, leaving five seats. The count and creation/registration need a repository-scoped lock or reservation so concurrent additions cannot bypass the new cap.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Point the launcher row at both closing tests**

This `closed` row covers both cap enforcement and the worktree-local hooks configuration, but its selector names only the cap test; that test can still pass if the `extensions.worktreeConfig` and `core.hooksPath` behavior is removed or implemented incorrectly. Include the separate hooks-path test in the disposition, or split the controls, so every behavior claimed as closed is actually checked.
